[00:58 - 1:41] capsulorhexis: The capsulorhexis is continued with forceps, while a Sinskey hook provides counter-traction. Due to severe lens mobility, four iris hooks are inserted through paracentesis incisions and used to engage the edge of the capsulorhexis flap, thereby stabilizing the entire capsular bag. [1:41 - 2:20] capsular tension ring (ctr) insertion: Viscoelastic is injected to perform viscodissection. Two PMMA capsular tension segments (CTS) are inserted into the capsular fornix, one inferiorly and one superiorly, to support the equator of the bag. The eyelets of the CTSs are positioned centrally for later fixation.
[2:20 - 3:07] phacoemulsification: After hydrodissection, a phaco probe and chopper are introduced. The dense, white nucleus is broken into quadrants using a vertical chop technique. The nuclear fragments are then emulsified and aspirated from the capsular bag, which is held stable by the previously placed iris hooks and capsular tension segments.
[3:07 - 3:18] cortical irrigation and aspiration (i/a): Following injection of viscoelastic, bimanual irrigation and aspiration cannulas are used to remove the remaining lens cortex from the equatorial fornix of the capsular bag. The capsular tension segments are clearly visible supporting the bag.

This process is repeated for both CTSs, creating suture loops for scleral fixation.
[4:18 - 4:28] wound hydration and closure: Using microforceps and a needle driver, adjustable slip knots are tied on the externalized Gore-Tex sutures. This allows for precise tensioning to center the entire IOL-capsular bag complex.
[4:28 - 4:40] capsular tension ring (ctr) insertion: A capsular tension ring (CTR) is injected into the capsular bag. A Sinskey hook is used to guide the trailing end of the CTR fully into the capsular fornix, providing 360-degree support.

[5:04 - 5:24] wound hydration and closure: The external slip knots on the Gore-Tex sutures are permanently locked. The knots are then carefully trimmed and rotated into the previously created scleral grooves/tunnels to bury them beneath the surface, preventing future erosion.

reference_narration:
[00:09 - 00:12] paracentesis creation: A side-port blade is used to create a paracentesis incision in the peripheral clear cornea, providing access to the anterior chamber.
[00:12 - 00:33] capsular bag inflation with viscoelastic: A cannula is inserted through the paracentesis to inject a clear ophthalmic viscosurgical device (OVD), deepening and stabilizing the anterior chamber.
[00:33 - 00:38] main incision creation: A keratome is used to create a multi-planar clear corneal main incision, which will serve as the primary entry point for surgical instruments.
[00:40 - 01:05] capsulorhexis: A cystotome is used to puncture the anterior capsule and create an initial flap. Capsulorhexis forceps then grasp the flap and guide it in a circular motion to complete a continuous curvilinear capsulorhexis (CCC).
[01:06 - 01:23] hydrodissection and nuclear rotation: A cannula is placed under the capsulorhexis edge, and balanced salt solution is injected to create a fluid wave, separating the lens nucleus and cortex from the capsular bag. The nucleus is then gently tilted to prolapse one pole out of the bag.
[01:23 - 01:26] viscoelastic injection for endothelial protection: A dispersive viscoelastic is injected into the anterior chamber to coat and protect the corneal endothelium prior to phacoemulsification.
[01:26 - 02:08] phacoemulsification: The phaco probe and a chopper are introduced into the eye. The tilted nucleus is engaged with the phaco tip. The chopper is used to split the nucleus into two halves. Each half is then emulsified and aspirated. Finally, the remaining epinuclear shell is removed.
[02:09 - 03:00] cortical irrigation/aspiration (i/a): An irrigation/aspiration (I/A) probe is used to remove the remaining soft lens cortex from the capsular bag, cleaning the equatorial fornix and posterior capsule.
[03:00 - 03:15] capsular bag inflation with viscoelastic: Cohesive viscoelastic is injected into the empty and clean capsular bag to create space and maintain its form for the upcoming intraocular lens implantation.
[03:15 - 03:36] intraocular lens (iol) insertion: A single-piece acrylic monofocal IOL is injected into the capsular bag using an injector system. A chopper is then used to tuck the trailing haptic into the bag and rotate the lens into its final position.
[03:37 - 04:08] viscoelastic removal: The I/A probe is used to thoroughly remove all viscoelastic from the anterior chamber, including from behind the IOL optic, to prevent post-operative pressure spikes.
[04:08 - 04:30] wound hydration and closure: A cannula is used to hydrate the corneal stroma at the main incision and paracentesis sites, causing localized swelling to create a self-sealing wound. A sponge is used to confirm there is no leakage.
